title: Cyber incident disrupting services for Pacific Blue Cross members | CBC News
html:
British Columbia

Cyber incident disrupting services for Pacific Blue Cross members

Burnaby-based health benefits provider says it’s investigating and working to restore its systems

Pacific Blue Cross says it's dealing with a "cyber incident" that has disrupted some of its systems, leaving members unable to access certain services, including its website and contact centre.

The Burnaby-based health benefits provider, which serves approximately 1.7 million British Columbians, says it first became aware of the disruption early Wednesday, Nov. 25.

"We have taken steps to contain the incident and we are working to securely restore services," the company said.

It says it has brought in external specialists to investigate the extent of the incident but has not disclosed what caused it or whether members' personal information has been compromised.

  • B.C. post-secondary application portal affected by data breach

  • More stories from Vancouver-South Coast

The company provides extended health, dental, life, disability, travel and other health insurance products.

It is asking members to hold on to their claims and receipts, as well as any plan administration requests, until the interruption is resolved. Those submissions will be processed once services are restored, the company says.

For emergency travel claims, members can contact Medi-Assist at 1-888-699-9333 from Canada or the United States, or call collect at 1-604-419-4487 from other countries.

The company has not said how many members are directly affected by the disruption.


CBC News has reached out to Pacific Blue Cross for more details.

The incident comes amid a series of cybersecurity breaches affecting Canadian businesses and public institutions in recent months.

Companies and organizations such as Bell, Staples Canada's printing website, KPMG and Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children have all reported cybersecurity incidents in the last few months alone.

  • Data breaches are coming fast and furious. Are businesses doing enough to protect your data?

  • So, your personal info was hacked in a breach. Here's how scammers use it against you

In B.C., a recent CBC News investigation found that a Russian ransomware group posted screenshots on the dark web from what appears to be a database stolen from the Burnaby School District.

Officials have said the massive data breach included medical information, detailed learning assessments, and personal information about both staff and students.

Earlier this month, personal information belonging to students in the Central Okanagan School District was compromised following a phishing email sent to students.

In October, Save-On-Foods notified members of its More Rewards loyalty program that personal information had been accessed following unauthorized activity on one of its servers.
